newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom increases ATM capacity.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom increases ATM capacity.

text.p: France Telecom said in a statement on Tuesday it would increase the capacity of its asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) network in France, used by Internet access providers, to 155 megabits per second in 1997 from the current 34 megabits.
The increase is the result of the installation of new high capacity switches -- Northern Telecom Nortel Passport 160 -- of which there will be 60 in France at the end of 1997.

It follows a big rise in the use of France Telecom's Transpac services which doubled in 1996 to 101,000 billion characters, mainly due to the rise of Internet services in France such as AOL, Microsoft's MSN and France Telecom's own Wanadoo.
Transpac is also part of Global Intranet, an intranet service offered by the Global One joint venture and its parents France Telecom, Deutsche Telekom and Sprint Corp.
